added_lines: parish newsletter 18th october 2026 twenty-ninth sunday in ordinary time no: 2066 mt 22:15-21 a visit to the eternal city! recently, i had the opportunity to travel to rome to attend the diaconate ordination of a young american seminarian. you may vaguely remember justin seidleck from two years ago when he participated in the holy week ceremonies of 2024 in olsd. we have a family connection! my grand aunt, marie morgan, from near abbeyleix emigrated along with a number of her siblings to philadelphia between the years 1911 – 1915. justin is the great- grandson of marie morgan. a re-connection with long lost family members living in america was reignited by a ‘letter arriving from america’ in 1984. thus began the renewal of family ties, culminating on the 1st of october when i attended the ordination ceremony in st. peter’s basilica. and, meeting justin’s parents for the first time! below, you will see that the weekend wasn’t only about praying and kneeling!. a lovely opportunity to meet up with fr. livui and fr. niroj, they asked me to send their kind regards to everyone in naas, sallins and two mile house. naas

great news! naas parish have been chosen for the live tv broadcast of the holy week ceremonies 2027 on rte 1 television, coming live from the church of our lady and st. david. this will be a wonderful recognition of the bicentenary of our beloved church. this great opportunity will need much cooperation from the entire parish and from all involved in the various areas of parish ministry. it will be a collective effort from both our churches: cim and olsd. advanced planning will start shortly!confirmation 2027 pictured here, are a class from scoil an linbh íosa, ballycane, starting off the series of retreats for confirmation candidates at solas bhríde last week. over the course of the next month children from our three parishes will participate in a retreat day which begins with mass and includes activities exploring the holy spirit in our lives and a pilgrim walk to st. brigid’s well. many thanks to trish o’neill and the youth ministry team for accompanying the young people on their journey.

29th sunday in ordinary time deacon: rev. liam dunne matthew 22:15-21 what bears god’s i mage in the first of three ‘conflict stories’, we read today that the pharisees are looking to jesus for advice on their taxes. they try to flatter him first, ironically by spe aking the truth about him, but the tone is still disrespectful. this is a dangerous situation because in an unlikely alliance, the pharisees have brought along the herodians with them. the herodians were great supporters of the roman empire, so tensions here would have been high. if jesus answers ‘no’ to their question about paying taxes to caesar he risks being reported to the roman authorities as a revolutionary; if he says ‘yes’ then he may be accused of colluding with the occupying empire and abandoning the people. jesus sees through their ‘malice’ and speaks truth to power. he invites us to explore another way, a third way, one that is not a revolt but neither does it lie down and submit to oppression. yes, do your civic duty, but do not forget what belongs to god; this overrides any political power. this is how one truly advocates for the kingdom of heaven in the here and now. in 2018 and again in 2019, pope francis met the ceos of the world’s major fossil fuel companies at the vatican. he reminded them that today’s ecological crisis threatens the very future of the human family and our common home. he told them that ‘a radical energy transition was needed to save our common home’ and that while ‘civilisation requires … not destroy civilisation.’ pope francis in not afraid to speak truth to power, urging these powerful corporations to go beyond merely exploring what needs to be done and actually concentrating on what needs to be done. embarking on this new path will generate new jobs, reduce inequality and improve the quality of like for all. being a follower of jesus means that we prioritise the values that jesus teaches so that we can be co-creators of t his wild and wonderful kingdom of heaven here on earth. copyright triona doherty & jane mellett. the deep end: a journey with the sunday gospels in the year of matthew (dublin: messenger publications, 2022).
